title: PREVENTING PRESSURE SORES
knowledge: Discusses the definition of pressure sores.
Identify purpose and importance of knowing the stages of pressure sores.
Discusses the proper step of preventing or minimizing pressure sore.
Discusses the Nursing Care in taking care of Patient with pressure Sores.
skills: Pressure sore assessment is done using the risk indicator scale.
Assessment is done and will be a part of patient's file.

Precautionary actions are considered:
    a. Utilizes pressure relief devices such as pillows, air mattress and heel and elbow
    b. There is an ongoing assessment and documentation of potential sites for early sign of skin breakdown
    c. Patient is repositioned every 2 hours
    d. Incontinence is managed effectively
    e. Patient's skin is applied on the potential sites.
Document in the Handover and Nurses notes in the Oasis Program.
attitude: Accept constrictive criticism as learning opportunity.
To be self-aware of limitation in knowledge and skills.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.

Ability to organize and facilitate a Reflection session in and on practice after the Standards in Ward Routine Discharge learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.

title: PULSE OXIMETER
knowledge: States the indications for using pulse oximeter.
States the nursing responsibilities in caring for patient with pulse oximeter.
Identifies the proper sites for checking the SPO2.
Identifies the factors or situations that may affect the pulse oximeter measurement.
Identifies the normal range of SPO2 and nursing actions needed if abnormal result.
Explains the contraindications and complications of pulse oximetery.
Explains the way of documenting the SPO2 on nurse's documents (OASIS).
Verbalizes the actions to be done if there is problem with the pulse oximeter.
States the indications for using pulse oximeter.
skills: Demonstrates the proper check-up before using the pulse oximeter.
Demonstrate precautions prior to application of pulse oximeter such as hand hygiene.
Demonstrates ability to recognize when improper sensor placement is affecting pulse oximeter reading.
Demonstrate awareness of device care, proper cleaning and disinfection.
attitude: Respect patient/ family life, dignity rights and safety.

title: STANDARDS OF ADMISSION
knowledge: Discusses guidelines for the general admission of the patient in the ward.
Identify purpose and importance of knowing the guidelines of admission.
Discusses the proper step of admitting patient.
skills: Prepares the room as soon as admission notification is received.
Common courtesy to the patients such as proper self-introduction to patient and family is observed.
Checked the admission records and patients form if complete and duly signed.
Checked doctor's order for admission in the Oasis Program.
Checked the patient's identification bracelet for the completeness of the Patient's name, MRN number, Age, Sex and nationality and date of admission.

Oriented the patient to the physical set-up and facilities such as use of call bell, side rails, lights, telephone, toilet, visiting time, hospital rules and regulations, meal schedules, patient valuables and others.
Completed the initial admission physical assessment of the patient.
Obtain vital signs and record in the Oasis Program.
Notify the attending physician regarding the admission and carry out admission orders according to priority.

Completed the routine admission procedure such as:
    a. Handover                       e. Admission Registry Book
    b. Bed Tag                         f. Diagnostic/ Diet request through OASIS
    c. Patient's Directory (checked OASIS)    g. Medication sheet, nurses notes, V/S
    d. Patient Census              h. Admission documentation
attitude: Accept constrictive criticism as learning opportunity.
To be self-aware of limitation in knowledge and skills.
Attentive to overall patient experience e.g. pain, anxiety and have ability to provide comfort and emotional support as needed.
Ability to organize and facilitate a Reflection session in and on practice after the Standards of Admission learning opportunity occurs and activates findings to improve future practice and response.
